title: Why my first pipeline turned red
body:
Today I pushed a small change and my pipeline turned red in less than a minute. At first I was upset. Then I read the log and found a missing comma.

A red pipeline is good news: the robot caught my mistake before any user saw it. I fixed the comma, pushed again, and the pipeline turned green.

Lesson for me: read the first red line of the log. It almost always tells the whole story.

title: Docker in one sentence
body:
Docker puts my app and everything it needs into one box, so it runs the same on my laptop and on the server.

The box is called an image. When I start an image I get a container. I can start ten containers from one image, and I can throw a container away without losing the image.

title: A day in numbers
body:
Cups of tea: 4. Red builds: 2. Green builds: 5. Lines of code written: about 120. Lines of code deleted: about 200, which felt better.

The most useful number of the day was 1: one small change at a time makes every mistake easy to find.

title: Five things I want to build
body:
A habit tracker. A tiny weather page for my city. A quiz about the things I am learning. A page that shows how my website is doing. And a bot that tells me when my build turns red.

I will start with the smallest one and deploy it with a pipeline, so that every idea becomes a real link I can share.
